children: 完全抽象掉存款货币出现的影响，非常图式化地说，国家控制对银行券有两个重要影响。第一，流通的进入点和退出点缩减为一个：中央银行。信用货币的流量始于并终于中央银行，并通过银行体系的合作获得规则性。特别是银行券向中央银行的回流，成为银行体系的常规业务之一：各单个银行把银行券集中起来，通过普遍化的票据交换体系送回中央银行。其直接结果是，银行券数量的决定获得某种稳定性和规则性，并受中央银行密切监督。

Abstracting entirely from the effects of the emergence of deposit money, and very schematically, state control has two significant effects on banknotes. First, the points of entry and exit from circulation are reduced to one, the central bank. The flows of credit money begin and end at the central bank and they are given regularity through the co-operation of the banking system. The reflux of banknotes back to the central bank, in particular, becomes one of the regular operations of the banking system as banknotes are concentrated by individual banks and channelled back to the central bank in a generalised system of clearing. The immediate result of this is a degree of stability and regularity in the determination of banknote quantity, closely monitored by the central bank.
第二，国家干预增大了操纵银行券流量的可能性。国家直接干预银行券发行，使信用货币数量与它所取代的黄金完全不成比例的可能性增大，从而导致价格名目的紊乱。在银行券占货币存量很大部分、且国家预算赤字促使其操纵信用货币发行的国家，这种趋势必然更加明显。因此，国家干预一方面加强了银行券的普遍性，另一方面增大了它固有的潜在不稳定性。

Second, state intervention enhances the possibility of tampering with banknote flows. Direct state interference with the issue of banknotes makes it more likely that the quantity of credit money would be completely out of proportion with the gold it replaces, thus leading to upsets in the nomenclature of prices. This tendency will inevitably be more pronounced in countries where banknotes are a substantial part of the money stock, and where the state runs budget deficits that encourage it to tamper with credit-money issue. Thus state intervention, on the one hand, strengthens the universality of the banknote and, on the other, increases its inherent potential instability.
现在我们可以转向存款制度中货币的支配职能，并为未来的工作指出一些指导线索。本文主张，存款货币对应于贮藏职能上升为支配地位。第一步是表明，银行券信用货币已经包含被完全观念性的对银行债权即存款取代的可能性。随后表明，基于分支银行制扩张的商业信用与货币信用衔接方式的变化，促成存款制度的确立。

We can now turn to the dominant function of money in the deposit system, and indicate some guidelines for future work. It is argued that deposit money corresponds to the elevation of the hoarding function into dominance. The first step is to show that banknote credit money already contains the possibility of being supplanted by entirely ideal claims on banks, i.e. deposits. Subsequently, it is shown that changes in the articulation of commercial with monetary credit, based on the expansion of branch banking, foster the establishment of a deposit system.

由银行券促成的交易，本质上以一般等价物躯体的观念性在场为前提。当银行券介入交换时，一般等价物的占有在参与者之间转移，但实际易手的却是无价值的银行券，即银行——哪怕是中央银行——的一纸支付承诺。这种交易潜在地包含着一种可能性：同样观念性地转移一般等价物，而不同时转移有形的支付承诺。原则上，对银行的债权可以不必采取银行券形式而转移。然而，这一可能性以具有社会意义的方式实现，并不直接来自交易本身的逻辑。要使这一可能性实现、使银行券被取代，银行体系必须成长到足以把货币的贮藏职能推上支配地位。

Transactions facilitated by banknotes are essentially premised on the ideal presence of the body of the universal equivalent. When banknotes intervene in exchange, possession of the universal equivalent is transferred between the participants but what actually changes hands is the valueless banknote, a mere promise to pay by a bank, even if it is the central bank. Contained potentially within the transaction is the possibility of an equally ideal transfer of the universal equivalent but without the simultaneous transfer of corporeal promises to pay. In principle, the claim on the bank could be transferred without it necessarily taking the banknote form. However, realisation of this possibility in a socially significant way does not follow directly from the logic of the transaction itself. For the possibility to be realised and the banknote to be superseded, the banking system has to grow sufficiently to propel the hoarding function of money into dominance.
货币贮藏是马克思货币理论的一个关键方面。与凯恩斯不同，马克思不把贮藏当作个人消费选择的余额即个人储蓄，而是当作资本积累的一个系统性方面。
两个例子足以说明这一点。当资本实现的利润超过即期再投资所需时，贮藏在结构上形成。当资本的流通时间缩短、从特定资本循环中释放资金时，贮藏再次形成。
对我们的目的重要的是，贮藏为货币信用和银行体系的成长提供基础。如前所述，银行把贮藏转化为生息资本，从而把货币送回实际积累。

Hoarding of money is a crucial aspect of Marx’s monetary theory. Unlike Keynes, Marx treated hoarding not as a residual of individual consumption choices, i.e. as individual saving, but as a systematic aspect of capital accumulation.

Two examples will suffice to demonstrate the point. Hoards are structurally formed when capitals realise profits in excess of what is required for immediate reinvestment. Hoards are again formed when the circulation time of capital is reduced, releasing funds from particular circuits of capital.

What is important for our purposes is that hoards provide the basis for monetary credit and for the growth of the banking system. As has already been said, banks turn hoards into interest-bearing capital, and so return the money to real accumulation.
从这一观点看，货币存款是随着货币贮藏被集中和贷出而产生的对银行的债权。

存款制度，即集中和利用暂时停滞货币的一般系统过程，以分支银行制的扩张为前提条件。银行必须能够广泛地伸入交换领域，才能维持一个集中贮藏的一般体系。正是这一发展，使银行券在发达资本主义中被取代、不再是主要的支付手段。有了系统性的贮藏集中，就可以观念性地转移货币，而不必让银行的支付承诺易手。支付可以改为直接转移对银行的债权，作为不同银行账户中的记账分录。其直接推论是，银行券乃至一切流通货币被挤出交换领域。就货币的职能而言，流通职能萎缩，贮藏职能占支配地位。存款货币如今作为货币“存量”，对应于这种支配地位。这一发展的潜力自19世纪40年代以来就已显现，但只有当银行体系的实际成长确立了贮藏职能在资本主义经济中的首要作用时，它才得以实现。
Viewed from this standpoint, money deposits are claims against banks which are generated as money hoards are concentrated and lent out.

Now a deposit system, i.e. a general systematic process of collecting and utilising temporarily stagnant money, relies on the expansion of branch banking as a precondition. Banks have to be able to reach extensively in the sphere of exchange in order to sustain a general system of collecting hoards. Precisely this development allows the supersession of the banknote as the chief means of payment in advanced capitalism. Given the existence of systematic hoard collection, it is possible to transfer money ideally and without the passage of bank promises to pay. Instead payments can be made by transferring the claims on banks directly as entries in different bank accounts. The immediate corollary of this is that banknotes, indeed all circulating money, are displaced from the sphere of exchange. In terms of the functions of money, the circulating functions are diminished and the hoarding function becomes dominant. Depository money, as money ‘stock’ now, corresponds to this dominance. The potential for this development has been apparent since the 1840s,
but it was realised only when the actual growth of the banking system established the primary role of the hoarding function in the capitalist economy.
同样，银行券被存款机制逐渐取代，也与信用实践的变化有关。图式地说，商业信用与货币信用的衔接经历了一场影响银行券作用的转变。汇票的衰落有充分的文献记载，其经典解释明确基于分支银行制的兴起。
贮藏集中体系的扩展，伴随着商业信用与货币信用的衔接从贴现汇票转向银行的透支和直接贷款。这一转变的迅速和有效程度，取决于银行体系的成熟度和深度。其必然推论是，私人创造的信用货币进入流通逐渐失去重要性。现在支付可以例如通过透支完成；这把日益受国家控制的银行券推到相对于存款机制的次要地位。

Equally, however, the gradual supersession of banknotes by the deposit mechanism is related to changes in credit practices. Put schematically, the articulation of commercial with monetary credit undergoes a transformation which affects the role of the banknote. The decline of the bill of exchange is well documented and its classic explanation has been explicitly based on the rise of branch banking.

The extension of the system of hoard collection is accompanied by a shift in the articulation of commercial and monetary credit away from discounting bills and towards overdrafts and direct loans by banks. How swift and effective the shift is depends on the sophistication and depth of the banking system. The necessary corollary of this is that the entry of privately created credit money into circulation gradually loses its significance. Payments can now be effected, for example, via overdrafts; this pushes the increasingly state-controlled banknote into second place relative to the deposit mechanism.

上述内容对现代存款货币的基本特征有什么含义？这里可以为研究方向确立一些重要的指引。第一，既然存款货币是由银行信用贷放生成的信用货币，对其数量决定的研究可以得益于我们已经就银行券信用货币数量得出的结论。内生因素，如货币信用和商业信用的周期性行为以及历史和制度现实，需要先行分析。其中最根本的，也许是资本主义积累生成货币贮藏的系统性结构趋势。此外，与利息率的联系问题，必须以比仅仅把利息率作为货币供给函数的一个自变量复杂得多的方式处理。恰恰因为信用货币数量的决定比真正货币更复杂，货币乘数及其不稳定性之类的问题，要求先研究信用与资本实际积累的衔接。第二，存款中介的路径概念（就“路径”能够确立而言），以及这种货币流通速度的性质，需要更密切的关注。存款货币的贷放与注销，即它在交换中运动的周期性，在文献中尚未得到充分研究。把这些与商业信用和货币信用的贷放和偿还系统地联系起来，很可能会就存款货币的数量得出重要结论。

What are the implications of the above for the fundamental traits of modern deposit money? Some important pointers for the direction of research can be established here. First, since depository money is credit money generated by the advance of banking credit, the study of the determination of its quantity would benefit from the conclusions we have already drawn on the quantity of banknote credit money. Endogenous factors, such as the cyclical behaviour of monetary and commercial credit as well as historical and institutional realities, require prior analysis. Perhaps the most fundamental of these is the systematic structural tendency of capitalist accumulation to generate hoards of money. Furthermore, the issue of the link with the rate of interest has to be dealt with much more complexly than by merely including the latter as an argument in the money supply function. Precisely because the quantity of credit money is subject to a more complex determination than money-proper, issues such as the money multiplier and its instability require prior study of the articulation of credit with the real accumulation of capital. Second, the concept of the path of depository mediation (insofar as a ‘path’ could be established), and that of the character of the velocity of such money, require closer attention. The advance and cancellation of deposit money, i.e. the cyclicity of its movement in exchange, have not been adequately studied in the literature. It is probable that the systematic linking of these to the advance and repayment of commercial and monetary credit would yield important conclusions with regard to the quantity of deposit money.
就现代银行券而言，随着存款货币和贮藏上升为支配地位，其性质发生根本变化。显而易见，银行券不再衔接商业信用与货币信用，并已被存款机制取代、不再是主要的支付手段。例如在英国，银行券已退化为单纯的流通手段职能，主要在私人收入支出领域便利商品交换。这一点由银行券中介的交易笔数众多、金额细小，以及银行券流通中反映私人消费季节模式的强烈季节性所确立。

当代资本主义流通中银行券的进入，在不受国家干预时，是由私人收入的支出引起的。银行券按照收入实现目的对货币的需求进入交换；因此其进入倾向于由需求决定。此外，回流倾向于发生在从私人收入中形成贮藏时，而不是在偿还对银行的债务时。个人从私人收入中创造贮藏，把银行券带回银行，转化为存款债权。银行体系把返回的信用货币流量集中起来，变成单一的、规则的流量，并把它导向中央银行、退出流通。存款信用货币兴起的结果，是削弱了现代银行券与信用贷放和偿还的联系。

As regards the modern banknote, a fundamental change in its character follows the rise of depository money and hoarding into dominance. It is immediately evident that the banknote no longer bridges commercial and monetary credit and has been supplanted as the chief means of payment by the deposit mechanism. Banknotes in Britain, for example, have been reduced to the function of simple means of circulation, facilitating primarily the exchange of commodities in the area of expenditure of private income. This is established by the multiplicity and small size of transactions mediated by banknotes, together with the strong seasonality in banknote circulation which reflects the seasonal pattern of private consumption.

The entry of banknotes into contemporary capitalist circulation, when not interfered with by the state, is occasioned by the expenditure of private income. Banknotes enter exchange according to how money is demanded for purposes of income realisation; hence, their entry tends to be demand-determined. Furthermore, the reflux tends to take place as hoards out of private income are created, and not as debts to banks are paid. Hoard creation by individuals out of private income brings banknotes back to the banks to be transformed into depository claims. The banking system concentrates the returning flows of credit money, turns them into a single, regular flow and directs the latter to the central bank and out of circulation. The upshot of the rise of depository credit money is to attenuate the links of the modern banknote with the advance and repayment of credit.

zh: 黄金在发达资本主义交换中的作用

children: The Role of Gold in Advanced Capitalist Exchange
本章迄今论证了马克思主义理论为解释货币形式的变化提供了系统的基础，而黄金是货币的一个关键原初形式。这里我们应当简要考察随着资本主义交换的发展黄金的作用。

It has so far been argued in this chapter that Marxist theory provides a systematic basis for explaining the changes in the form of money, and that gold is a crucial original form of money. At this point we should briefly consider the role of gold as capitalist exchange develops.
国内流通信用货币兴起的一个直接结果，是把黄金排挤到交换领域之外的贮藏中。取决于银行体系的发展程度，黄金贮藏倾向于被银行体系作为首屈一指的贮藏集中者所集中。马克思认为黄金贮藏既有国内作用也有国际作用。
黄金贮藏的国内作用是在危机时刻支撑信用和货币体系：黄金作为支付手段总是被接受的；因此它总能化解货币危机。然而，信用货币的发展及其基于银行业（尤其是中央银行业）日益成熟而向存款货币的进一步演化，降低了黄金的国内重要性。马克思已经注意到，苏格兰与英格兰相比正是这种情况。
稳定的银行体系在危机中能够越来越多地自行提供支付手段，或以银行券形式，或以存款信用形式。结果，黄金贮藏被缩减到其对外的世界市场作用。

One immediate result from the domestic rise of circulating credit money is to displace gold into hoards outside the sphere of exchange. Depending on the degree of development of the banking system, the gold hoards will tend to be concentrated by the latter as the hoard collector par excellence. Hoards of gold were seen by Marx as having both a domestic and an international role.

The domestic role of the gold hoard is to bolster the credit and monetary system in time of crisis: gold is always acceptable as means of payment; hence, it can always resolve a monetary crisis. However, the development of credit money and its further evolution into deposit money, based on growing sophistication of banking (central banking in particular), reduces the domestic significance of gold. Marx had already noted that this was the case in Scotland in contrast with England.

A stable banking system can increasingly provide its own means of payment in a crisis, either as banknotes or as depository credits. The gold hoard, as a result, is reduced to its external world market role.
马克思论证说，在世界市场上，货币作为“世界货币”执行职能，充当国际接受的支付手段。这必须是黄金，因为货币的民族特性必须在世界市场上被抛弃。因此，马克思通常把黄金外流看作“世界货币”的流动，由对国外的支付债务引起，这些债务在外汇市场的正常运行中不容许用信用清偿。
各国必须支付黄金来结清国际收支债务、购买急需的粮食、进行战争等等，这些职能在危机时期尤为突出。对我们的目的有趣的一点是，按照马克思，参与世界市场的国家必须拥有黄金贮藏，其规模表明一国应对世界市场波动、保护其政治权力的能力。

In the world market, Marx argued, money functions as ‘world money’, as the internationally acceptable means of payment. This has to be gold, since the national peculiarities of money have to be shed in the world market. Marx’s view of gold drains, as a result, was typically as flows of ‘world money’, invoked by payment obligations abroad which would not admit of credit settlement in the normal operation of the foreign exchange markets.

Gold had to be paid by countries to settle balance of payments debts, to buy urgently required food supplies, to fight wars, and so on, functions particularly pronounced in times of crisis. The interesting point for our purposes is that, according to Marx, countries participating in the world market had to have a gold hoard, the size of which indicated a country’s ability to face up to the fluctuations of the world market and to protect its political power.

于是，黄金在资本主义交换中的残余作用问题，变成了参与世界市场各国的国际贮藏的演化问题。可以有益地类比国内市场黄金贮藏的演化。黄金的世界作用，与信用体系的国际化以及银行跨国提供存款货币的能力成反比。只要信用生成的支付手段在国际上扩散，黄金贮藏就倾向于只在信用体系受到严重震荡、货币作为货币必须现身时才被使用。这通常发生在大商业危机、战争、自然灾害之类的时候。结果将是黄金流动的作用递减，这种金属越来越多地被禁闭在国际贮藏中。此外，黄金贮藏的国际分布将反映不同民族国家在世界市场上权重的变动，并将保持强烈的政治性质。

The question of the residual role of gold in capitalist exchange thus becomes a question about the evolution of the international hoards of countries participating in the world market. A parallel can usefully be drawn with the evolution of gold hoards in the domestic markets. The world role of gold depends inversely on the internationalisation of the credit system and the ability of banks to provide depository money across frontiers. Insofar as credit-generated means of payment proliferate internationally, the gold hoards will tend to be used only when the credit system has been severely shaken and money as money has to appear. This will typically happen in a major commercial crisis, a war, a natural disaster, and the like. A diminishing role for gold flows and the increasing confinement of the metal in international hoards will be the result. Furthermore, the distribution of gold hoards internationally will reflect the shifting weight of different nation states in the world market, and will retain a strong political character.
本章的主要理论关切是货币各种形式之间质的区别。我们把这些区别与货币在交换中被主要要求执行的职能联系起来。更具体地说，经济理论通常假定，凡是充当交换手段的东西就是货币。货币流通职能的重要性不容否认，但在发达的资本主义流通中，支付职能和贮藏职能更为重要。货币主要是金属、银行券还是存款，取决于哪种职能占支配地位。因此，银行券和存款分别对应于支付手段和贮藏手段职能。

The main theoretical concern of this chapter has been the qualitative differences among the various forms of money. We related these differences to the functions that money is primarily called upon to perform in exchange. More specifically, economic theory usually assumes that money is anything that functions as means of exchange. The importance of money’s circulating function cannot be denied, but in developed capitalist circulation, the paying and hoarding functions are more significant. Whether money is primarily metal, banknotes or deposits depends on which function is dominant. Thus banknotes and deposits correspond to the functions of means of payment and means of hoarding, respectively.
马克思提出的货币理论为系统分析货币形式提供了框架。在这一框架内，价值尺度、交换手段、支付手段和贮藏手段职能在交换发展的不同水平上起支配作用。据此，我们为货币的基本形式即黄金推导了一个货币数量恒等式。这一恒等式不同于费雪版本和剑桥版本，因为它承认对货币的流通职能和支付职能有不同的内生影响，以及货币执行各自职能时有不同的流通速度。

The theory of money proposed by Marx provides a framework for systematic analysis of the forms of money. Within this framework, the functions of measure of value, means of exchange, means of payment and means of hoarding play the dominant role at different levels of the development of exchange. With this in mind, a Quantity of Money identity was derived for the fundamental form of money, i.e. gold. This identity is distinct from the Fisherian and Cambridge versions in that it recognises the different endogenous influences on the circulating and paying functions of money as well as the different velocities of money in the performance of the respective functions.
在资本主义特有的交换中，货币的流通职能逐渐失去重要性，而贮藏职能变得更加重要。与此相应，银行券对应于支付手段职能而不是狭义的交换手段，存款货币则对应于贮藏手段职能。我们把银行券和存款称为“信用货币”，以强调信用关系对其性质的决定作用。信用体系生成的货币依靠信用过程进入和退出交换，这赋予它特有的循环路径，我们在银行券的情形中已经较为详细地看到了这一点。

In specifically capitalist exchange, the circulating functions of money gradually lose their significance, while the hoarding function becomes more important. In accordance with this, banknotes correspond to the function of means of payment, rather than to narrow means of exchange, while deposit money corresponds to the function of means of hoarding. We called banknotes and deposits ‘credit money’ in order to stress the determining role of credit relations in their characterisation. Money generated by the credit system relies on credit processes for its entry and exit from exchange and this gives it its characteristic circular path, as we saw in some detail for banknotes.

这些结论对当代资本主义分析的含义是重要的。对现代存款货币的研究必须从支撑它的信用关系开始。考察实际积累创造贮藏的结构趋势，以及这些贮藏转化为生息资本的基本机制，是研究现代货币行为的前提条件。银行信用与商业信用的相互作用以及信用体系的制度发展，塑造信用货币的供给与注销。因此，存款信用货币决定的内生性研究，不能被表述为对利息率的简单函数依赖。事实上，在最基本、高度抽象的层面上，利息率不必作为决定性的影响出现在分析中。完整考察与存款相关——并在更远一层与世界货币相关——的贮藏职能，是为了充分刻画现代资本主义货币中介而有待完成的工作。

The implications for the analysis of contemporary capitalism are significant. The study of modern deposit money has to commence from the credit relations which underpin the latter. Examination of the structural tendency of real accumulation to create hoards, and the fundamentals of the transformation of those hoards into interest-bearing capital, are preconditions for the study of the behaviour of modern money. The interaction of banking and commercial credit and the institutional development of the credit system shape the supply and cancellation of credit money. Thus the study of the endogeneity of the determination of deposit credit money cannot be posed as a simple functional dependence on the rate of interest. Indeed, at the most basic and highly abstract level, the rate of interest need not appear in the analysis as a determining influence. The complete examination of the hoarding function as it relates to deposits – and, at a further remove, to world money – is work that remains to be done in order fully to characterise modern capitalist monetary mediation.
